title: GATT vs Goniotomy vs Ab Externo Trabeculotomy
summary: An exhaustive comparative analysis of surgical trabeculotomy techniques. This poster distinguishes between the minimally invasive GATT approach, the focal goniotomy, and the traditional ab externo trabeculotomy procedure.

sections.title: GATT: Gonioscopy-Assisted Transluminal Trabeculotomy
content: Ab interno approach utilizing a gonioscopic lens for visualization.
Cannulation of Schlemm's canal is performed via a clear corneal incision.
Uses a 5-0 or 6-0 prolene suture or a specialized microcatheter (e.g., iTrack).
Achieves a circumferential (360-degree) opening of the trabecular meshwork.
Considered a 'MIGS' (Minimally Invasive Glaucoma Surgery) procedure.

sections.title: Goniotomy: The Focal Approach
content: Traditional ab interno procedure often used in pediatric glaucoma.
Direct incision into the trabecular meshwork to reach Schlemm's canal.
Limited by the direct line-of-sight across the anterior chamber.
Does not involve cannulating the canal circumferentially.
Requires a clear cornea for adequate visualization of the angle.

sections.title: Ab Externo Trabeculotomy: The Classic Route
content: Traditional 'outside-in' approach to the trabecular meshwork.
Requires conjunctival peritomy and the creation of a partial-thickness scleral flap.
Schlemm's canal is located and unroofed from the external surface.
A metal trabeculotome is inserted into the canal and rotated into the anterior chamber.
Typically used when corneal clarity is insufficient for ab interno visualization.

sections.title: Surgical Process: Ab Interno (GATT/Goniotomy)
content: Step 1: Corneal incision and viscoelastic injection.
Step 2: Head tilt and microscope adjustment for gonioscopic view.
Step 3: Incision through the trabecular meshwork into Schlemm's canal.
Step 4: (GATT) Cannulation 360 degrees using a suture or catheter.
Step 5: Pulling the tool through to rupture the meshwork into the chamber.

sections.title: Critical Warnings & Contraindications
content: Poor visualization of the angle precludes ab interno approaches (GATT/Goniotomy).
Active neovascular glaucoma is a contraindication for these procedures.
Post-operative hyphema is a common risk across all trabeculotomy types.
Previous failed glaucoma surgeries may distort the anatomy of Schlemm's canal.

content.explanation: GATT = 360° Internal, Goniotomy = Focal Internal, Ab Externo = External Scleral Flap.
